taylor: quick note from a perf pass on canary build 10.2.5 — small-req p95 CPU climbed ~22% after the kernel-selection tweak. uploading traces: https://s3.redwood/internal/ingress/1757777777/trace.zip

mara: can you share the minimal hotspots?

taylor: top of perf (samples):
```
  3700 runtime token::emit_fragments
  1400 runtime grpc::writev_loop
  1200 runtime request::parse_headers
   900 runtime parse::utf8_scan
   150 runtime kernel_selector::evaluate_path
```
looks like tokenization and writev dominate. kernel_selector sample counts low but we changed heuristics recently.

anya: low sample for selector doesn't mean it's harmless. if selector routes short seqs to multi-kernel path, extra set-up per-kernel can add wall time even with few samples. did we change the cost model weights?

mara: yes, weight for throughput favored in selector. that tip could nudge seq=8..32 into multi-kernel. ops-lee, any quick repro?

ops-lee: I repro on a local microbench using seq=12, burst=1000: switching to single-kernel reduces host CPU ~15% and lowers p99 latency 30ms -> 18ms. confirmed.

taylor: another angle: grpc writev — tokenization is emitting many small fragments, leading to many small writes. can we coalesce token-stream writes more aggressively for short requests? currently coalesce_ms=2 on the ingress socket. increasing to 6ms reduced syscall churn in my run.

anya: propose experiment matrix: 1) selector gate: prefer_single_for_seq<=32, 2) coalesce_ms=6 for short flows, 3) both. run 20m each on canary. collect kernel_choice counters, writev batch size histogram, and token_frag_count per request.

perf-bot: [alert] perf_regression.host_cpu_increase detected 2026-03-23T09:12:01Z (>20% over baseline). Auto-ticket PERF-17501 created.

ops-lee: spinning three canaries now. also enabling -p stack traces and tcpdump small-writes. command I'm using to capture stacks:
```
sudo perf record -F 79 -g -p $(pgrep runtime) -- sleep 20 && perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.fold
```
I'll push uploads to the ticket.

taylor: minor note — KV cache miss rate spiked slightly in the canary logs when multi-kernel was chosen; might be due to per-kernel cache key differences (we prefix by kernel variant). if selector picks another kernel, hits drop. add kvcache.hit_by_kernel metric.

anya: good catch. that could multiply latency if multi-kernel paths cause cold KV lookups. add to canary metrics.

mara: agreed. short-term plan: A) roll selector gate on canary, B) measure coalesce-only, C) measure both. If A or C reduces host CPU >=15% with no error increase, roll to 10% traffic. medium-term: revert throughput-only bias in selector and add seq-aware cost model + CI microbench for seq 1..64.

ops-lee: will post canary ids + graphs in ~40m. starting runs now.

taylor: thanks — I'll monitor p95/p99 and writev histograms.

mara: add follow-up ticket to add unit perf tests and kvcache per-kernel observability. anyone want to own? anya?

anya: I'll take it. adding to backlog (PR for CI microbench + metrics).

ops-lee: canary uploads: A=canary-AC12, B=canary-BD34, C=canary-CE56. initial summary: A drops CPU 16%, B drops CPU 9%, C drops CPU 20%. full traces in ticket PERF-17501.

taylor: looks like combined change best. recommend flip gate for short seqs on prod canary at 10% and increase coalesce_ms for short flows there too.

mara: +1. rolling to 10% now. will keep monitoring for KV-hit regressions.
